correctness.rationale: Products of the two signed monomial branch Jacobians place 2^Cj on the three singular axes; equal-measure branches give a lazy clockwise 3-state random-walk occupation law. The tilted matrix D_u(I+S)/2 has determinant equation (2λ-u)(2λ-1)^2=u; for u>0 its Perron root is simple, positive and analytic. Setting y=2λ-1 gives u=y²(1+y)/(1+y²), λ=(1+y)/2 and x=d log λ/d log u=y(1+y²)/(y³+3y+2), with strictly positive derivative and endpoint range (0,1). The finite-state additive LDP then yields I(x)=x log u - log λ; union bounding the three coordinate events gives the largest/least singular-value tails. Finite-prefix boundary path estimates give I(0)=I(1)=log2, not inferred from finite simulations. The polynomial benchmark identity f_u((u+2)/3)=-4(u-1)^3/27 and Perron monotonicity prove strict comparison of tilted pressures; variational arguments transfer to strict left/right rate ordering. Independently symbolically checked cubic, Legendre derivative and benchmark factor, plus numerical sign at four tilts. The Gaussian covariance equality is an acknowledged prior fact.

final_claim: Under Lebesgue initial data for the fixed 3D twisted baker map, the n-step largest/minimal singular-logarithm tails have explicit speed-n rate I parametrized by u=y²(1+y)/(1+y²), x=y(1+y²)/(y³+3y+2). Rates are strictly above iid three-box benchmark below mean 1/3 and below it above mean, despite identical Gaussian covariance.
